cards.text: Friend, the kingdom just split in two. Jeroboam son of Nebat is the new king over Israel, while Rehoboam, Solomon's son, rules Judah. Jeroboam builds up Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, moves in, then heads out and builds Penuel too.

cards.question: New king, new cities. But Jeroboam has a worry he only says in his heart. What does he think might happen to his kingdom?

answers.text: It might go back to the house of David
It might be taken over by Egypt
It might be split among his sons

cards.text: He plays out the whole worst case in his heart, friend. The house of the LORD is in Jerusalem, and that's where the people go up to offer sacrifices.

cards.question: Jeroboam says if the people go up to sacrifice in Jerusalem, their ___ will return to Rehoboam king of Judah.
True or false: Jeroboam thinks the people might kill him and go back to Rehoboam.

cards.text: So after seeking advice, the king comes up with a fix. He makes something. Two of them, actually.

cards.question: What does Jeroboam make after seeking advice?

cards.text: Then Jeroboam tells the people, “Going up to Jerusalem is too much for you.” Look at him, friend, SO worried about everybody's feet.

cards.question: What does Jeroboam tell the people the golden calves are?

answers.text: The gods who brought them out of Egypt
Signs that the LORD chose Jeroboam
Guards to keep the land of Israel safe

cards.question: Jeroboam sets one golden calf up in ___ and the other in ___.

cards.text: And the Bible says it plainly: “this thing became a sin.” The people walk as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves.
Hold up, Jerusalem was “too much,” but walking as far as Dan is NO problem? That's calling in sick to work, then driving four hours to wait in line at a theme park.
Jeroboam isn't done. He builds shrines on the high places, and shrines need priests.

cards.question: Who does Jeroboam appoint as priests for his shrines?

answers.text: People from every class who aren't Levites
Only Levites who came up from Judah
Only elders who once served Solomon

cards.text: Next up, a feast. Jeroboam ordains one on the fifteenth day of the eighth month.

cards.question: True or false: Jeroboam's feast is like the feast that was in Judah.
At his feast, Jeroboam makes his offering in ___ to sacrifice to the calves he set up.
True or false: The month of Jeroboam's feast is a month God chose.

cards.text: So there he is in Bethel, offering sacrifices and burning incense at the feast he ordained for the Israelites. Hang on, friend, because this story is far from over.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 quotes "this thing became a sin.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from outside the passage: the kingdom split, Jeroboam is king over Israel (1 Kings 12:20), and Rehoboam, Solomon's son, rules Judah (1 Kings 11:43; 12:17). It gives no reference for any of them and cites only 1 Kings 12:25.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke and a callback to 1 Kings 12:28 and 12:30. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward, so it works as a recap. The joke should ride along on card 11, which tells 12:30.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The sarcastic line "Look at him, friend, SO worried about everybody's feet" mocks Jeroboam. It doesn't laugh with his human situation, and Papa Dorin isn't the target of the joke.

rule.text: **Humble.** When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: Most story cards (1, 3, 6, 13, 15, 19) are plain retelling with little of Papa Dorin's voice. The walkthrough has only two attempts at a laugh. Several moments could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, such as Jeroboam playing out the worst case in his heart, appointing priests from every class, or picking a month of his own choosing.

rule.text: Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
